meta.title: Diesel overfill of tank T-101 during night transfer
meta.team: Lead investigator; Operations superintendent; Instrument technician; HSE adviser
meta.description: During a night ship-to-tank transfer, diesel overflowed from tank T-101 into bund B-1. About 14 m³ was contained in the bund and recovered; no injuries and no off-site release.
meta.conclusion: The transfer was not stopped because the level gauge LT-101 froze at 78 % and the single night-shift operator, busy with a ship arrival, did not cross-check the level. The independent high-high trip LSHH-101 failed because its float was seized; proof testing had dropped out of the maintenance system. The independent alarm LAH-102 was probably missed in an alarm flood (still being confirmed).
meta.lessons:
Independent overfill protection is only independent if it is tested.
Manning changes need a management-of-change review that covers peak workload, such as a ship arrival during a transfer.

top.label: Diesel overflowed from tank T-101 into the bund during a night transfer
top.evidence: About 14 m³ diesel in bund B-1 at 03:40 (shift log, CCTV, photos P1–P9). Bund held; no off-site release.

e0.label: Ship-to-tank transfer into T-101 under way (demand on the overfill controls)
e0.evidence: Transfer TR-2611 from MV Coral started 22:10.

prob.note: About one transfer a week into T-101 (2025 transfer records).

g2.label: Transfer not stopped before the tank was full
g2.evidence: Pumping continued until 03:38, when the ship stopped on radio call.

g4.label: Operator unaware the tank was nearly full
g4.evidence: Operator interview: believed level was 78 % at 03:20.

g8.label: Level gauge LT-101 indicated lower than the actual level
g8.evidence: DCS trend flat at 78 % from 01:55 while dip showed 100 %.

e4.label: LT-101 servo gauge displacer stuck (frozen reading)
e4.evidence: Gauge found stuck at 78 % on inspection; displacer wire fouled with wax (photo P12).
e4.why: Gauge not in the planned maintenance system after the 2024 replacement.

e9.label: LT-101 calibration drift
e9.evidence: Calibration certificate 6 weeks old; as-found check within 2 mm.

g7.label: Operator did not cross-check the level by an independent means
g7.evidence: No radar or dip cross-check recorded in the 4-hourly round.

e3.label: Level cross-check not done during the transfer
e3.evidence: Round sheet blank for 02:00; operator was at jetty 2 for MV Delta arrival.
e3.why: Transfer procedure has no hold point for cross-checking level near the end of a transfer.

prob.note: HEART D nominal 0.09 raised for night shift, single operator handling a ship arrival (EPCs: time shortage, high workload).

h1.label: Single operator on night shift, also handling a ship arrival
h1.evidence: Roster: one operator 18:00–06:00; MV Delta berthed 01:50.
h1.why: Night manning reduced from two to one in 2025 without a management-of-change review.

e5.label: Transfer nomination larger than available ullage (planning error)
e5.evidence: Nomination 2 400 m³ against 2 610 m³ ullage: calculation checked and correct.

g3.label: Independent overfill protection did not stop the transfer
g3.evidence: No trip of XV-101 recorded; LAH-102 alarm acknowledged at 03:12.

g9.label: High-level alarm LAH-102 did not lead to the transfer being stopped
g9.evidence: Alarm at 03:12; pumping stopped 03:38 (26 min later).

g5.label: High-high level trip LSHH-101 / XV-101 failed
g5.evidence: XV-101 stayed open; LSHH-101 did not change state when flooded.

e6.label: LSHH-101 level switch failed on demand (float stuck)
e6.evidence: Float found seized by corrosion product (photo P15). Last proof test 30 months ago (CMMS).
e6.why: Proof testing of tank overfill switches dropped from the CMMS schedule; no tracking of overdue SIS tests.

prob.note: Library 0.01 assumes an annual proof test; LSHH-101 test was 18 months overdue, so PFD scaled up about ×5.

e7.label: Trip left bypassed after maintenance
e7.evidence: Bypass log and DCS event list: no bypass active on LSHH-101.

e8.label: Control-room operator did not respond to the independent high-level alarm LAH-102
e8.evidence: LAH-102 acknowledged at 03:12; 41 other alarms in the same 20 minutes (preliminary journal).
e8.test: Retrieve alarm journal 02:30–03:40 and interview control-room operator about alarm load.
e8.why: Alarm flood during ship arrival; LAH-102 has the same priority as nuisance alarms.

e10.label: Stop instruction to the ship by radio not received or delayed
e10.test: Obtain the jetty and ship VHF recordings for 03:10–03:40; interview the ship duty officer.

actions.text: Restore proof testing of all tank overfill switches (LSHH) in the CMMS and test LSHH-101/201/301 within 14 days.
Add an overdue-SIS-test KPI to the monthly management review.
Add servo gauge LT-101 (and sister gauges) to the planned maintenance system with a 6-monthly displacer inspection.
Add a level cross-check hold point (radar vs servo, at 85 % and 95 %) to the transfer procedure.
Carry out a management-of-change review of single-operator night manning during ship arrivals.
Re-prioritise LAH-102 and other independent overfill alarms as high priority; rationalise nuisance alarms.
